name: Hexenwasser Söll Hohe Salve
kurzbeschreibung: Hexenwasser in Söll: Tyrol's oldest and multi-award-winning mountain adventure park at 1,150 m with barefoot trail, bee house, and witchcraft stations.
beschreibung:
Overview

The award-winning Hexenwasser Söll Hohe Salve is situated on the sunny slopes of the Hohe Salve above the village of Söll in the Tyrolean Unterland (Kufstein district) at an altitude of approximately 1,150 metres. Opened in 2002 as Austria's first alpine summer adventure park, this nature-oriented area around the middle station of the Bergbahn Söll cable car has developed into one of the most prestigious excursion destinations in the Alps. Under the guiding theme of “marvel, grasp, and understand”, Hexenwasser encourages visitors of all ages to explore the wonders of the alpine mountain world directly with all five senses.

Route & Requirements

The centrepiece of the expansive park is the famous, approximately two-kilometre-long barefoot trail: on varied surfaces—from soft moss, stream pebbles, and bark mulch to mud pools and smooth river stones—visitors train their sense of touch and experience the revitalising effect of natural reflexology. Along the rushing mountain stream, more than 60 lovingly designed activity and adventure stations invite participation: children dam watercourses with sluices, make singing water bowls vibrate, or explore the mechanisms of historic water wheels. A cultural and natural highlight is the Bienenhaus (bee house): equipped with observation beehives and a humming dark corridor, beekeepers demonstrate the indispensable ecological role of the honeybee and offer visitors tastings of fresh forest honey. In the ancient Simonalm—a 400-year-old farmhouse faithfully relocated here—visitors bake traditional farmhouse bread together and listen to authentic Tyrolean witch legends. The mystical Hexenmuseum (witch museum) and the herbal gardens harmoniously round off the diverse range of experiences.

Visit & Arrival

Hexenwasser Söll is open daily during the summer season from mid-May to late October from 08:45 to 17:30. Admission to the Hexenwasser grounds is free—visitors only need a cable car ticket for the Bergbahn Söll up to the middle station. Summer 2025/2026 fares: ascent and descent on the Hexenwasser gondola for adults approx. €27.00, youth (born 2007–2009) approx. €20.50, children (born 2010–2019) approx. €13.50, children under 6 ride free. With the regional Kitzbüheler Alpen Sommer Card, cable car rides are included without limit. By car: via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Kufstein Süd or Wörgl Ost), onto the B178 (Loferer Straße) directly to Söll; large free parking areas are available at the valley station of the Bergbahn Söll (Stampfanger 21). By public transport: ÖBB trains to Wörgl or Kufstein station, from where the VVT bus line 4060 runs every half hour directly to the Söll Bergbahn stop.

Tips

The 10-seater Hexenwasser gondola and the main trails around the middle station are barrier-free, wheelchair accessible, and easily navigable with all-terrain pushchairs. Bring a change of clothes and small towels for children for the barefoot and water trail. Combine your day with an onward ride on the Keatbahn lift to the 1,829 m summit of the Hohe Salve with its famous pilgrimage church.
